items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I bought them all Duke's records, bought them home, and put the, I had a portable, phonograph with a photograph, right up by the piano, and I sat down at the piano and played with the thing. And I found out that he was taking the G7 chord... So I knew enough of music, you know, and I said, oh, and I

ctx.x: He went to Europe, you know.

That's right, he went to Europe, that's right. He went to Europe and the next year, Paschal, who used to play with Henderson. Paschal came in, Paschal got the band, he hired me as banjoist and ranger. Oh, I had made some arrangements for King's band, and incidentally, this might seem humorous, one of the boys came up to me and said, have you heard Red Nichols and Biff Moe play Ida, Sweeties Appleside? I said, yeah, I got the record. He said, why don't you steal that arrangement, arranging for the band. I said,…
A very progressive band, yes. A young Chicago kid.
